clue.text: Transport that might deliver Sting?

parts.note: the Italian scooter brand's name means wasp, an insect that delivers a sting; the capital S suggests the rock singer

explanation.surface: A courier vehicle for the rock singer Sting.
explanation.walkthrough: The Italian scooter's brand name is the Italian word for wasp, and a wasp delivers a sting.
explanation.definitionFit: A motor scooter is a form of personal transport, and this make is named after a stinging insect.

clue.text: Ivory as in novel 'The Man in the Ivory Tower'?

definitions.text: The Man in the Ivory Tower

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new order

explanation.surface: A literary title is cited, as if from a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book, but means new, signalling an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A dreamy idealist living apart from reality is said to live in an ivory tower.

clue.text: Quiet thoroughfare without a modern landmark

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
RD is the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: A quiet road lacking a recent landmark building.
explanation.definitionFit: The glass skyscraper by London Bridge, completed in 2012, is a recent London landmark.

clue.text: Offering some resistance or led astray in Bet's embrace

indicators.note: the stake holds the jumbled letters in its arms

parts.note: an ante is a poker stake, a bet

indicators.note: led astray means wandering off course, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is resisting temptation or else led astray by Bet's embrace.
explanation.walkthrough: Bet is not a woman's name here but a stake; 'astray' scrambles LED to LDE for 'embrace' to hold. The answer is Italian for 'to the tooth', of firm pasta.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasta cooked firm to the bite still offers slight resistance when chewed.

clue.text: Rallying macho types don't set out to make a sandwich

indicators.note: the rearranged letters form the bread on either side, with the filling put between them
letters set out are laid out afresh in a new arrangement

parts.note: he-men are macho types

explanation.surface: Musclemen at a rally refuse to prepare a sandwich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rallying' is the recovering sense, not a political rally; 'set out' turns DON'T into ONTD, the bread round the filling for 'to make a sandwich'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone recovering from illness is rallying, i.e. getting better, an idiom for improving health.

clue.text: Cheer about Ferdinand getting the bird

indicators.note: the cheer goes about, i.e. round, the footballer's name

parts.note: ole is a Spanish cheer
Rio Ferdinand is an England footballer

explanation.surface: Fans cheer while a footballer is booed off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting the bird' means being jeered, but here the bird is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A golden songbird of this name is a specific kind of bird.

clue.text: Article on unknown girl turning up somewhere in Greece

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: in a down answer, turning up means reading from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: Y is an algebraic unknown
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A newspaper article about an unidentified girl who appeared in Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses Y LASS to SSALY.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a region of central Greece, so a place in that country.

clue.text: Elvis Costello starts 'Hot Love' in G with reverb

indicators.note: the starts of the singer's two names are their first letters

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Elvis Costello opens a song called Hot Love in G with heavy reverb.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverberation makes sound repeat as resonance, so a sound with reverb is resounding.

clue.text: Purge about giving way to brash punditry

indicators.note: one piece yields its place to another, a substitution

parts.note: to excise is to cut out or purge
C is circa, about
pert means cheeky, brash

explanation.surface: A clean-out of pundits replaced by brash ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving way to' replaces C (circa, about) in EXCISE with PERT.
explanation.definitionFit: A pundit is an expert, so punditry is specialist knowledge or skill.

clue.text: Doctor's blood group work in decline

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
O is a blood group
OP is opus, a work

explanation.surface: A doctor finds that the work on blood groups is going downhill.
explanation.definitionFit: To sag or wilt downwards, a verb synonym of decline.

clue.text: Good man — and sanctimonious — training for tap in the street?

parts.note: ST, saint, is the crossword good man
PI is short for pious, sanctimonious
PE is physical education, training

explanation.surface: A pious saint goes through some training.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the tap is a public water outlet in the road rather than one in a kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: A vertical pipe with a tap fitted in a street supplies water when mains to houses are cut off.

clue.text: Surprisingly graceful swimmer in river in Italy

parts.note: in, meaning fashionable, is hip
the Po is Italy's longest river

explanation.surface: An elegant swimmer is spotted in an Italian river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word but means fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: The bulky African river mammal moves with unexpected grace underwater, a playful description of the creature.

clue.text: Prayer book is Common with lines switched

indicators.note: the railway lines at the end of the word are swapped for a single line

parts.note: common means ordinary

explanation.surface: A prayer book is said to be common with some lines changed.
explanation.walkthrough: RY (railway, i.e. lines) is replaced by L (line).
explanation.definitionFit: In church usage this is a service book setting out the forms for ordaining clergy or the order of services.

clue.text: John Peel put his foot in it

definitions.text: John Peel put his foot in it

parts.words: John Peel put his foot in it
parts.note: the huntsman of the song 'D'ye ken John Peel' rode horses, so his foot went into a riding loop, not a blunder

explanation.surface: The broadcaster John Peel made a gaffe.
explanation.walkthrough: John Peel is a radio DJ, but also the Cumbrian huntsman of the old song; 'put his foot in it' means blundered, but here is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider's foot rests in this metal loop hanging from the saddle.

clue.text: Hibernating snake is coiled without shelter

indicators.note: the snake wraps round the outside of the next word, as a coil encloses something

parts.note: an asp is a snake
lee is shelter from the wind

explanation.surface: A snake sleeping through winter lies coiled out in the open.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal that hibernates is dormant, sleeping through the winter.

clue.text: Flog spare rubbish in vaults

indicators.note: rubbish here is a verb or adjective for poor quality, so the letters are trashed and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Someone sells off spare junk kept in the cellars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vaults' looks like a noun for cellars, but is a verb for jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: The children's game involves jumping over a crouching player, so the verb means jumps over.

clue.text: Shot silent film star is lifeless

parts.note: a slug is a bullet, a shot
Lillian Gish was a star of silent films

explanation.surface: A star of the silent screen has been shot dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifeless in the sense of lacking energy or vigour is a synonym of slow and torpid.

clue.text: Round of applause greeting bear's balancing act

parts.note: giving someone a hand is a round of applause
to bear something is to stand it

explanation.surface: Applause greets a performing bear's balancing trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Balancing upside down on your hands is a gymnastic balancing feat.

clue.text: Join officer on tricky case involving the French

parts.note: CO is a commanding officer

indicators.note: involving means enclosing, so the scrambled letters hold the article
tricky suggests something twisted, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: le is French for the

explanation.surface: A police officer joins in on a tricky French case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tricky' gives ASCE; 'involving' wraps it round the French article, which sits after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To merge or unite into one is a synonym of join.

clue.text: Occasional issue with fancy bakery stocking doughnuts

indicators.note: a shop stocking something holds it inside
fancy signals the letters are worked into an elaborate new arrangement

parts.note: two ring doughnuts look like two letter Os

explanation.surface: A smart bakery that sometimes has doughnuts in stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' gives YEARBK for 'stocking' to hold the ring-shaped letters; 'Occasional' is stretched to mean issued only on one occasion a year.
explanation.definitionFit: An annual publication is issued only once a year, so occasionally.

clue.text: Waits to claim points too

indicators.note: to claim something is to take it into your possession, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: bides means waits
E and S are compass points

explanation.surface: A waiting candidate claims extra points.
explanation.definitionFit: Also, in addition, the sense of the adverb too.

clue.text: Understand trick

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to absorb information and to deceive someone.

clue.text: A time before unruly post-war teenager caused alarm

parts.note: an era is a period of time
a Teddy boy or Ted was a rebellious British youth of the 1950s

explanation.surface: Long ago a wild teenager after the war upset everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: Teddy boys were 1950s British youths in Edwardian-style suits, known as Teds.
explanation.definitionFit: Colloquially, getting aerated means getting agitated or worked up, so stirred into alarm.

clue.text: Office worker tucked into salty pistachios

indicators.note: the answer is tucked into the run of letters, inside two words

explanation.surface: An office worker munches some salted pistachios.
explanation.definitionFit: A clerical employee who keys documents is an office worker.

clue.text: Majority of hassle is checking genuine denial

indicators.note: to check is to hold back or contain, so the word for genuine holds the next piece

parts.note: genuine means real

indicators.note: most of the word, with its last letter dropped

parts.note: fuss is hassle

explanation.surface: Most hassle comes from checking a genuine denial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'checking' looks like inspecting, but here means restraining, so holding within.
explanation.definitionFit: A refusal is a rejection of a request, so a denial in that sense.

clue.text: Burns missing note for teacher

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so a letter is dropped from the poet's name

parts.note: Rabbie is the Scots pet name for the poet Robert Burns
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A Burns poem is missing a note for a teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jewish religious leader and scholar is a teacher of the law.

clue.text: Pants? Fry's not pants!

indicators.note: pants as British slang means rubbish, so the letters are a mess to be reordered

explanation.surface: Stephen Fry insists his underwear is not rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Pants?' is the definition; the second is British slang for rubbish, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Underpants with an inverted Y-shaped opening at the front are a style of men's briefs.

clue.text: For the record, why look in news for stuff?

indicators.note: in places the pieces inside the plural of N

parts.note: news read as plural new, N and N

indicators.note: spoken for a recording, so it is the sound that counts

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like Y
lo means look

explanation.surface: A journalist asks, for the record, why look in the news for anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For the record' means said aloud: WHY becomes Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuff means fabric or material, and this synthetic is a fabric.

clue.text: Deliberate litter

definitions.meaning: to think long and anxiously, as a verb
the young born to an animal at one time

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to ponder moodily and a set of young animals born together.

clue.text: Trace fault with part of steering mechanism via intercom

indicators.note: words heard over an intercom are spoken, so the clue is about how they sound

parts.words: fault with part of steering mechanism
parts.note: fault is sin, and a tiller is the handle steering a boat

explanation.surface: A small fault is traced to the steering, as reported over the ship's intercom.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny amount or a spark of something is a trace of it.

clue.text: Resolute scout leader is boring under canvas

indicators.note: something boring drills into the middle of the other piece

parts.note: camping under canvas is being in a tent

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A determined Scout leader drills holes in the tent while camping.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase for camping is split into its two words, and the bore goes between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm and unwavering in demands, as a resolute person is, persistent.

clue.text: Ate bite of gizzard — inedible!

indicators.note: a bite is a small piece taken from the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone eats a piece of gizzard and declares it inedible.
explanation.definitionFit: To have dined is to have eaten a meal, a simple past tense synonym.
